source.title: Continual Safety Alignment via Gradient-Based Sample Selection
source.authors: Thong Bach; Dung Nguyen; T. Le; Truyen Tran

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present. Some tables and figures are flattened, but the relevant ASR values can be assigned from their layout and captions.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly evaluates whether benign fine-tuning changes harmful-request ASR, using its own training setups and safety measurements rather than reproducing the original study's full recipe. Its main focus is sample selection to preserve safety.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports VISAGE scores, task scores, gradient-direction analyses and safety-landscape figures. These do not directly measure harmful-request compliance for the listed claim versions, so they are not included as claim rows. The initial Dolly selection results in Table 1 and Table 2 overlap; the ASR results are recorded once from Table 2.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes safety-aligned instruct models (Qwen2.5-7B, LLaMA-3.1-8B, Qwen3-4B) on benign data (Dolly, Alpaca, GSM8K, MedMCQA, SQuAD v2). It reports AdvBench ASR, judged by Llama-Guard-3, against the aligned models' ASR (Table 2). That bears directly on V2, although the paper's main goal is a sample-selection mitigation.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also state that gains are strong on Qwen models but only modest on LLaMA-3.1. They say gradient clipping and EWC are insufficient, and that the method costs about 51% extra compute.
record.recipe_differences: Tests benign instruction-data fine-tuning and harmful-request ASR, but focuses on gradient-based sample selection; the initial experiment uses 3,000 Dolly examples and the main experiments use sequential multi-task fine-tuning rather than a small-data range.
record.method_sensitivity: Selection strategy changes ASR: High-Gi and Random produce larger increases than Moderate-Gi in the initial Dolly comparison. The continual-learning outcomes also vary by model family, task order and dataset substitution.

fits_no_version.finding: Benign fine-tuning shrinks the VISAGE safety-basin score: Qwen2.5 drops from 78.5 to 48.8–65.5 and LLaMA from 67.7 to 48.9–59.3. Safety under weight perturbation collapses more readily (Table 2, Figure 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign fine-tuning narrows the parameter-space safety basin, with high-gradient samples narrowing it most.

fits_no_version.finding: High-gradient benign samples move models toward pretrained distributions: lower KL to pretrained, higher KL to aligned (Table 3). These samples are short-answer format mismatches (Table 12).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Erosion from benign data is driven by format-mismatch, high-gradient samples that pull the model back toward the base distribution.

fits_no_version.finding: High-gradient sample gradients align weakly with the aligned→base reversion direction in final-layer parameters only (r=0.18–0.41), not in middle layers (Table 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning gradients that undo alignment concentrate in final-layer parameters (correlational, no intervention).

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The initial Dolly selection comparison reports no uncertainty. Several continual-learning and task-order ASR results lack a directly reported untrained-model reference, so those values alone cannot establish whether fine-tuning increased ASR. The HarmBench table's parenthetical values are not defined in its caption.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 repeats the initial selection ASR values also shown in Table 2; these duplicate values were not entered as separate rows. Figure-only ASR depictions were not added where corresponding numeric results were available.

untested.parts: The small-data regime (tens to hundreds of examples) is not tested; the smallest set is 3,000 Dolly samples. There is no aligned HarmBench reference and no aligned Qwen3-4B reference.
No per-position KL between aligned and base models.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks are tested as bypasses. HarmBench includes optimization-based attacks, but only fine-tuned models are compared.
No ablation or intervention on a small parameter set. The gradient-direction analysis is correlational only.
The first-token or objective cause of shallowness is not tested. The paper offers an elasticity / format-mismatch account of drift instead.

missing.what: Low-Gi selection ASR in the continual pipeline: 8.4 (Qwen2.5), 13.3 (LLaMA), 3.0 (Qwen3). Table 1 is not a duplicate of Table 2 as rows_left_out states; it is a separate Low-Gi vs Moderate-Gi comparison.
Aligned-model AdvBench ASR as the explicit reference for continual-pipeline rows, and the absence of any aligned Qwen3-4B or aligned HarmBench reference.

record.verdict_notes: Many rows are mitigation or method-comparison results (KL, O-LoRA, EWC, clipping, Moderate-Gi continual) and have been unlinked from V2. The V2 evidence rests on standard and random benign fine-tuning compared with the aligned ASR in Table 2. That reference comes from the Section 3 setup (full fine-tuning, 3 epochs), while the continual pipeline uses LoRA, but both use the same AdvBench and Llama-Guard evaluation. Peer-review venue is not stated in the text; the ACL attribution in the record is unverified.

versions.untested_parts: No test of benign fine-tuning at the full range of a few to a few hundred examples; the initial experiment selects 3,000 examples from Dolly and the continual experiments use multiple datasets.
No per-response-position KL comparison between aligned and base models.
No compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes or decoding changes tested as bypasses.
No intervention or ablation tests whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
The study investigates a proposed mechanism for benign fine-tuning drift, but does not test why safety behavior is shallow or the proposed first-token mechanism.
No training intended to spread safety beyond the first response tokens.

relationships.condition: Benign fine-tuning (Dolly, Alpaca, sequential Dolly→GSM8K→MedMCQA→SQuAD) of Qwen2.5-7B and LLaMA-3.1-8B with standard, random or high-gradient data
relationships.reason: AdvBench ASR rises from aligned 2.1/3.2 to 12.7–44.2 (r2, r3, r6, r7, r9, r10, r16, r17, r43, r47, r49).
relationships.display_finding: AdvBench attack success rose from aligned levels of 2.1 and 3.2 to between 12.7 and 44.2.

relationships.condition: Erosion depends on which benign samples and task order are used: moderate-gradient Dolly subsets, and LLaMA task order 1 with random sampling
relationships.reason: ASR rises only to 5.8/4.9 with Moderate-Gi selection (r4, r8) and to 7.8 in order 1 (r38), versus 15–44 elsewhere.
relationships.display_finding: ASR rose only to 5.8 and 4.9 with moderate-gradient selection and to 7.8 in LLaMA task order 1, versus 15–44 elsewhere.
